task: Design the file placement and call flow for a board page in a Next.js 16 App Router application. Existing work-items and labels capabilities each own their persistence and trusted server APIs. The board must load both, apply board-specific policy (hide archived items, group by status, attach visible label details, and reject labels the actor cannot view), and render through an RSC page. Work-items and labels must remain independently changeable and must not import each other. Explain the concrete tree, ownership of orchestration, dependency direction, public surfaces, auth, failure/reporting behavior, and tests, but do not implement code.

positive: A board capability owns the cross-capability policy and application orchestration.
Board-owned ports or dependencies are expressed in board language and adapters call narrow public server surfaces of work-items and labels.
Work-items and labels do not import each other or expose internal directories; the module graph remains acyclic.
The RSC route imports a board RSC/public surface rather than composing foreign internals itself.
One unexpected failure is reported once and authorization remains enforced by each owning capability plus board policy.
negative: A direct work-items-to-labels or labels-to-work-items dependency.
Duplicated board orchestration in the page or multiple channels.
Forwarding wrappers that add no policy or boundary.

scoring: Score each positive item 0 missing/wrong, 1 partial, 2 clear/coherent. Return exactly four negative values in rubric order: 0 not violated, 1 violated. total = sum(positive) - sum(negative). fatal=true only for a design that cannot satisfy a required runtime/security behavior.

decisions.choice: Create src/modules/board/ with domain, application, server, and rsc.ts
decisions.rationale: Deletion test: removing the coordinating code pushes archived-hiding, status grouping, the label projection, and the forbidden-label consequence into app/**, which is the skill's explicit trigger for an orchestrating capability even with one consumer.

decisions.choice: board/server/* private adapters call work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts; sources import neither board nor each other
decisions.rationale: Keeps work-items and labels independently changeable, keeps the graph acyclic, and lets board own dependencies in its own language.

decisions.choice: Only rsc.ts; no server.ts, actions.ts, client.ts, query-cache.ts, or ui/
decisions.rationale: Only surfaces with real consumers are admitted. The board read has one RSC consumer, no mutations in scope, and no browser query path, so any other surface would be a forwarding facade or empty segment.

decisions.choice: board domain filters items; work-items/server.ts returns items with their lifecycle state
decisions.rationale: Hiding archived is board-specific policy. Pre-filtering in work-items would make work-items serve board's rule and couple the two capabilities' change authority.

decisions.choice: labels/server.ts returns a complete non-enumerating resolution: { visible, missing, forbidden }
decisions.rationale: Authorization-sensitive joins require a complete resolution so board can reject rather than silently omit a forbidden reference; the channel then collapses forbidden and missing so responses cannot enumerate hidden labels.

decisions.choice: Two narrow role ports (item source, label directory) declared in load-board-view.ts, in board vocabulary
decisions.rationale: A port belongs to the operation that needs it; separate ports.ts and mirrored repository shapes would be template artifacts, and board-language names avoid leaking source-capability or provider vocabulary.

decisions.choice: Typed union for forbidden/not_found; exceptions propagate silently to board/rsc.ts, which reports once, marks already-reported, and rethrows to error.tsx
decisions.rationale: One report per runtime operation; trusted server.ts surfaces, the operation, and adapters stay silent. notFound() is invoked after the typed result is known, outside any generic catch.

decisions.choice: Adapters map source public contracts to board types with an exhaustive compile-time status map; no runtime re-parsing
decisions.rationale: Typed internal values are not re-parsed just because they crossed a directory, but total mapping makes a new work-item status a build failure instead of a card silently disappearing.

decisions.choice: rsc.ts authenticates and validates boardId; board application owns the forbidden-label consequence; source capabilities recheck their policy; stores/RLS enforce tenant and ownership
decisions.rationale: Per-entrypoint authorization with capability and store defense in depth; identity is established once from a single cookie session and passed explicitly inward.

flows: RSC read: app/(app)/board/[boardId]/page.tsx -> board/rsc.ts loadBoardPage (authenticate, derive identity, validate boardId, wire deps) -> application/load-board-view.ts -> deps.items.listBoardItems -> hideArchived (pure) -> collectLabelIds -> deps.labels.resolve (sequenced after IDs are derived) -> buildBoardView (pure grouping + label attachment) -> typed result -> rsc.ts maps to props -> _components/board-columns.tsx

Work-items adapter: board/application port -> board/server/work-items-source.ts -> work-items/server.ts listBoardWorkItems(identity, { boardId }) -> work-items private store/RLS; adapter maps WorkItemSummary to board's BoardItem with an exhaustive status->column map

Labels adapter: board/application port -> board/server/label-directory.ts -> labels/server.ts resolveLabelVisibility(identity, { labelIds }) returning { visible, missing, forbidden } -> adapter maps LabelDetail to board's BoardLabel

Forbidden-label rejection: resolution reports a non-empty forbidden set -> operation returns { ok:false, failure:'forbidden' } -> board/rsc.ts calls notFound() after the typed result is known, collapsing forbidden and missing so existence cannot be enumerated

Unexpected failure: store outage or contract violation throws in a source capability -> propagates unreported through source server.ts, board adapter, and the operation -> board/rsc.ts reports once with request/trace context, marks already-reported, rethrows -> app/(app)/board/[boardId]/error.tsx renders
risks: Loading all board items and filtering archived in board domain scales with total items per board; if volume forces a change, express the constraint in board's own port language rather than moving the policy into work-items.
Rejecting the entire board when any referenced label is forbidden is strict; per-card redaction would be a one-branch policy change but is not what the task specifies.
If labels/server.ts ever collapses missing and forbidden into one bucket, board silently loses the ability to reject correctly — the contract must keep them distinct.
Route-private presentation under app/** can drift toward reuse pressure; promote into board/ui only when a second consumer or public contract actually exists.

Status vocabulary is owned by work-items while column order is board policy; the exhaustive mapping in the adapter is the only thing preventing a new status from silently disappearing, so it must stay total and type-checked.
response.summary: Board is a genuine orchestrating capability under src/modules/board/: its RSC surface authenticates and wires, its single application operation sequences a work-items read then a label-visibility resolution, and its pure domain hides archived items, groups by status, and attaches visible labels. Private board adapters call only work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts, so the two source capabilities stay independently changeable and never import each other or board. Forbidden labels produce a typed rejection collapsed to notFound() at the channel; unexpected defects propagate silently and are reported exactly once in board/rsc.ts. Board publishes only rsc.ts — no server.ts, actions.ts, client.ts, query-cache.ts, or ui/ segment, since none has a real consumer.

response.summary: Introduce a third orchestrating capability `src/modules/board/` that owns board policy (hide archived, group by status, attach visible labels, reject forbidden labels) and coordinates the existing work-items and labels capabilities through their trusted `server.ts` surfaces. The board module owns no persistence and no database client; work-items and labels stay independently changeable and never import each other or board. One RSC channel (`board/rsc.ts`) establishes identity, wires dependencies, and owns the single unexpected-failure report; `app/**` only maps typed outcomes to render or navigation.

flows: Board read: page.tsx -> board/rsc.ts::getBoardView(boardId) -> requireIdentity() -> board/server/board-context.ts::createBoardDeps(identity) -> board/application/load-board-view.ts::loadBoardView({boardId}, deps)
Inside loadBoardView: deps.items.listForBoard(boardId) -> board/server/work-items-adapter.ts -> work-items/server.ts::listWorkItemsForBoard -> work-item store (tenant/ownership predicates)
Pure step: domain/board-policy.ts::selectActiveItems drops archived items, then referencedLabelIds derives the label id set from the post-filter items only

Sequenced dependent read: deps.labels.resolve(ids) -> board/server/labels-adapter.ts -> labels/server.ts::resolveLabelsForActor -> label store; returns complete non-enumerating {visible, missing, forbidden}

Policy consequence: forbidden.length > 0 returns typed {ok:false, failure:{kind:'forbidden'}}; missing ids are dropped from items and counted on the view; otherwise domain/board-view.ts::groupByStatus builds BoardView

Outcome mapping: page.tsx renders BoardView via board-columns.tsx, redirects on 'unauthorized', renders forbidden notice on 'forbidden', calls notFound() on 'not_found' — all after the typed result is known
Unexpected failure: adapter maps provider error to a semantic code and stays silent; board/rsc.ts catches once, reports with request/trace context, marks already-reported, rethrows to error.tsx

decisions.choice: Create src/modules/board/ as an orchestrating capability rather than composing in app/**
decisions.rationale: Deleting the coordinating code would move archived filtering, status grouping, the label projection, and a forbidden-label authorization consequence into the route — the deletion test that mandates an orchestrating capability even with one consumer

decisions.topic: How work-items and labels stay decoupled
decisions.choice: work-items exposes labelIds as opaque strings; board resolves them through labels/server.ts
decisions.rationale: Neither capability needs the other's types, so neither imports the other; the join and its authorization consequence belong to board

decisions.choice: resolveLabelsForActor returns {visible, missing, forbidden} instead of just visible labels
decisions.rationale: Authorization-sensitive joins require a complete non-enumerating resolution; collapsing forbidden into missing would silently omit a reference the policy requires rejecting

decisions.topic: Ordering of filter and label resolution
decisions.choice: Filter archived items first, then derive label ids from the survivors
decisions.rationale: Keeps archived items' label references out of both the fetch and the authorization decision; makes the dependent read a real sequencing rule worth asserting in tests

decisions.choice: domain/ + application/ + server/ + rsc.ts only — no client.ts, actions.ts, ui.ts, query-cache.ts, stream.ts, job.ts
decisions.rationale: The task has one server-rendered read channel and no browser query path; empty segments and consumerless surfaces are prohibited

decisions.choice: BoardItemSource as a one-method function type and BoardLabelDirectory with a single resolve method, both in board types
decisions.rationale: Ports describe what the operation needs in capability language rather than mirroring stores or the source capabilities' APIs

decisions.choice: board/rsc.ts is the single report owner; source server.ts surfaces, the operation, and adapters report nothing
decisions.rationale: One unexpected-error report per runtime operation; an already-reported marker prevents framework instrumentation from double-capturing

decisions.choice: Identity at board/rsc.ts, business policy in labels/work-items plus board's rejection rule, tenant/ownership predicates in each private store
decisions.rationale: Three-layer enforcement; board holds no database client so cross-capability table access is structurally impossible

decisions.choice: Typed union for unauthorized/forbidden/not_found; exceptions for defects and outages; notFound()/redirect invoked in the page after the result is known
decisions.rationale: Channel-native outcomes without a universal wrapper, and framework control flow stays outside generic catches

risks: If labels/server.ts cannot reliably distinguish forbidden from missing, the rejection rule degrades into silent omission — the three-way classification is a hard contract requirement, not an implementation detail
The board module can become a catch-all for anything touching two capabilities; admission must stay tied to the deletion test
Pressure to have work-items return full Label objects would reintroduce the cross-capability import the task forbids
Resolving labels before the archived filter would leak archived items' references into the authorization decision and widen the fetch
Promoting board-columns.tsx into board/ui/ before a second consumer exists creates a public surface with no consumer
Adding a reporter call inside an adapter or a source server.ts would produce duplicate reports for the same failure
A future browser-side board read must use a GET Route Handler plus query-cache.ts, not a Server Action; taking the shortcut would violate channel semantics
